paragraphs: What I love and hate about vibe-coding: you come up with 2 tasks, and then you sit and wait for 246 to get finished.
While Claude does them, I keep slowly playing with features. Compared to Claude, Codex of course has simply no features at all, in principle =))))

Just plugged in an always-on terminal session with root, nailed to a Telegram bot. On top of that I installed Whisper V3-turbo so the model catches even a mumbling sleepy voice, even the gasping voice of some … hardcore runner, even the sacred voice of a man whose mouth is busy with a beer.
And I stuck the most fashionable new modern stylish … TTS in the world on top. Because surely I'm not going to read what it coded for me, right.

I understand that many in the chat have long used these features and are used to them, but for me, walking the dog and shipping a couple of features via “hey Siri” without touching any devices with my hands — that was akin to a spacewalk =)
… of course edge-tts's playful Svetka, I'm …)))))))))))))))))))))))))
So can you recommend genuinely peppy free TTS engines with decent Russian? =)))
Or if those don't exist, screw Russian, at least with … English then)
So, the … reasons all the startup founders who rushed to urgently make money on … vibe-coding are flopping were listed back in the last century by the mustachioed singer Igor Nikolaev.
There was a checklist of certain reasons:
1) The first reason is you.
2) And the second — all your dreams.
3) The third is all your words, I barely believed them.
4) The fourth reason is a lie, who's right and who's wrong, you can't tell.
5) The fifth reason is pain, because love has died.
But those aren't the reasons Uncle Gena was thinking about, face-planting … into the salad while getting drunk to “Old Songs About the Main Thing.”
THESE ARE THE REASONS FOR VIBE-CODER ….

The only thing I don't understand in this scheme is how Nikolaev managed to peer through the space-time continuum so far that he described the entire market of vibe-coder projects so Socratically flawlessly?
Think about it yourselves:
The first reason is the coders themselves. They've … common sense so thoroughly that WITH THE HELP OF AN LLM they build APIs that ANOTHER LLM CAN'T UNDERSTAND.

Honestly, it can't even always read them. Because humanity has invented … in the spirit of pretty multi-button multicolored … such complex, multilayered variations on how to depict an API that even though a living person in his right mind will never again go study some vile API with his own eyes, they keep creating APIs in exactly the form where models simply physically can't read them in full on the first pass.

I swear to you — 4 out of 5 APIs of the services I tried to integrate end up unreadable in full by an LLM on the first, second, and sometimes eighteenth pass. Are you … smoking cottage cheese over there, you … artists?
Make a … huge button, API FOR LLMs, and in plain text … your wretched 150 … endpoints in there. Is that so hard to think of?
But that's not all.

You see, if you have 150 … endpoints listed in a row, and their entire description is their … worthless NAME, the LLM won't get anywhere. A coder you can push, over ten trips to the JOHN, to sit and solve your riddles and send bash requests trying to pick first the right endpoint for the task at hand, then the set of parameters, and then the … syntax for requesting those parameters.
An LLM is a much smarter creature, which is why it thinks far more simply and logically.

It thinks: … quite a swamp of … endpoints here, what kind of party did I wander into, well, I'll take these ones then and tell my human that everything was found and I built a … working system in 15 hours, and then if he doesn't like something I can just tell him he's absolutely right and go back for a new portion of random endpoints. I don't … care, I have no other tasks anyway. Humans like to … around, who am I to stop them.
But endpoints usually exist to perform some function.
I'm sure most endpoints don't exist for that, of course, but we're talking about services you can at least find. Their endpoints should, in theory, point their tips toward money.
If an endpoint has a function, that function can be described. Not in formulas of higher astrophysics, but SIMPLY … IN WORDS … FOR CRYING OUT LOUD.
The joke is that if you simply tell the LLM, like, … goddess of love, could you please make sense of our system as follows:
We have code that lets something happen.

You're the smartest and unsurpassed, so you can understand really well from the code what it does, why anyone might need it, and in general tell anyone about every function and every feature of it. The problem is that nobody but us has access to our code, that's our little prank. However, we give people indirect access to suck on our code to their heart's content. For that we have … API endpoints, which by the way you made yourself, you sweet little ….

Can you now write a school essay on the topic “… each endpoint is needed for, and exactly how best to use them so that specifically what comes out, and how not to, so that it definitely doesn't come out”?

The truly mightiest of this world will even think to ask to … in half a dozen examples of using different parameters, just like in the children's encyclopedia “What Is What.” Only without pictures; we're not going to … show an LLM pictures in JSON, it WON'T SEE THEM ANYWAY.
You're wincing like, Tim's gotten carried away, he's overdoing it now, but I … recently saw code snippets as images … in API docs …!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

And that's it. Imagine a lamer like me pokes his LLM into your API, so-called documentation, and instead of the usual … there, the model straight up says: oh — this is exactly what we need! I'll build it all for you now, by the way this software is good because of this and that, since thanks to it we…
Why the … am I explaining other people's systems to my LLM, … their creators' mothers?
What else did Nikolaev prophesy?
… everyone these days has half their endpoints dead and half undocumented?

You've vibe-coded yourselves to the point where you can't simply, I don't know, at least set up a triggered automaton that, along with gitleaks, would run through your … API and check whether we're deprecating or renaming or rolling out new naughty endpoints that absolutely must make it to the front page?
You could do that at least out of self-love, so you never have to think about such … tedium again?!?

And since I don't understand so much of what's listed above, how could I understand why the … you …, and call your latest dim-witted half-crawler “enrichment,” without even thinking of such simple things as deduplicating the results of your … data output? Seriously, I tried … 10 (!!!!!) startup data-search APIs — not a single … one thought to offer a setting so the same data doesn't sneak into requests again.
SURELY I HAVE A USER ID IN YOUR SYSTEM

So now I'm going to sit and build a deduplicator on my side so as to pay you thirty times for the same data, never knowing how much fresh stuff there'll be in each thousand results, and then also sit on my server deduplicating the result of those repeated … payments. Like I'm ….
I'm tired of writing this text, because it's very unpleasant to write about such ….

But in the end this is the main reason I sit and build everything of my own. Maybe in other niches things are better, but in the sales-data-enrichment-mailing-… niche there's simply nobody to pay money for a PARTNERSHIP. A partnership is when, in exchange for money, they take a piece of work off your hands by providing a service with functionality A/B/C/… and some understandable SLA range for each item you pay money for — not when you sit there puked-on for your own cash and pray, and then every 3 days the whole system falls apart because something fell over again, they renamed an endpoint again, a parameter, a path …, etc. And they explain it to you through their teeth as if you personally … that endpoint of theirs.
And talking about this with the creators of all these little softwares is useless, because they are practically all and always CODERS.
Coder-brain can do a lot, but it can't simply put itself in another person's place, though without that you'll never sell anything except by accident.

Think about it: I've been sitting there telling a heap of teams, like, … why have I been … with your … for a WEEK and it still doesn't work and doesn't work. Do you understand why? Want a hint? Because none of you even thinks to open a fresh clean OS on a VM and walk your customer's path trying to set everything up with an LLM. You won't … manage it, because if you managed it, I'd manage it too, and I wouldn't be … my brains here for a week corresponding with you.

So far the counter reads exactly zero. Exactly zero coders I've fought with over the last 3 months simply tried to jam their own … in somewhere with an LLM. All the … is only on the landing pages: AI-first, AI-native, LLM-driven, and other dumb ….

And of course I tell them this, but for some reason they start feeding me excuses instead of just doing this elementary action and being very surprised that it turns out to be simply impossible. Without the whole ecosystem that got built up around them during development, to which nobody but them has access from outside.

How do you not understand that this is the single most important advantage, both marketing and product, and how … it'll affect LTV, and conversion. This should be the new ISO, the new SOC 2 for products of the LLM era. Not just “we have an API,” but “our API can actually be embedded in a working process BEFORE the carcass goes cold.”
You could simply write on the landing page:

We're so … tuned for LLMs that even a … like Tim built an integration on top of our … in 2 hours with no coding knowledge at all. That's exactly where you need to move your products in 2026. Proud that you ship 30 new endpoints a week thanks to vibe-coding?
So what the … are they for if you can't jam them anywhere with that same vibe-coding?!?!?!?!!?!?!?!?!?

Respected people said they unsubscribed from me because they can't read about vibe-coding anymore (((((((((
I feel I went wrong somewhere in life, but where?!?

Well, my sweet Saturday style icons, I've finally finished the main part of what I've been vibe-coding for the last … knows how many weeks or months or years — I've lost track. Tonight is the first night in a long time that I slept peacefully, like the dead.
Now I can slowly return to normal life, to streams, interviews, breakdancing, Ultima, maybe even play some Dota!!!!!!!
Life is getting better.
I'll finish off the cosmetic stuff and on a separate stream show what the thing I built looks like and what will happen there next.

By the way, OpenAI's latest changes sort of hint at what I dreamed of: the model now seems to have no limits at all on executing a task. Apparently the latest price changes (everyone noticed it got more expensive and is getting more expensive still) let OpenAI unclench and let people get more from the models without resistance.

Before, I had to spend a lot of energy to burn through all the limits of the $200 subscription usefully rather than stupidly. It took a colossal number of prompts, and the behavior pattern itself — “we stop not when we're done but when OpenAI won't let us continue” — meant you needed 50 times more prompts, because complex tasks required dozens of approaches, then dozens more approaches to debug themselves, then dozens more to debug the seams with other systems and subsystems, then dozens more for optimization, which spawned new bugs both inside and at the seams…….
Now the model … away for 3–5 hours on a single prompt, and sometimes does more useful work than it used to in dozens of hours and fifty prompts.

For those who build landing pages or Telegram bots this may be unnoticeable, but if you were already building something very complex, on a stack of 5 languages, with … knows what labyrinths between front end and back end, you simply couldn't fail to notice it.

Bottomless context in a single session plus the above = the model now works exclusively 24/7, with no downtime at all. In the morning I throw just 5 complex prompts into the future in two parallel sessions (10 total), and in general the next time I'll need to throw in something new is in the evening at best, or deep at night — that's how it works now.
And that's great.

I once said earlier that OpenAI would arrive at the point where we simply say what we want to work, and how, and until it works exactly that way the model will …, maybe for several days, maybe a week.
That's the direction everything is developing in, for good.
For truly nimble work on a single project you now need 3 GPT PRO subscriptions at $200, meaning normal serious development simply costs $600 a month now.

I suppose the next model will make it go up to around $800, and that's how they'll smoothly bring us to the spend they need, controlling so that user churn doesn't eat the benefit of the inflow of new revenue. If it starts eating it — they'll widen the model lineup to satisfy more or less everyone. But those who know how to make money in business will always use the max tier, and I think by the end of this year they'll have learned to charge those people $2k.

Claude, by the way, lags far behind on this point. Mythos had better show up already. Honestly I would have unsubscribed from Claude by now if not for the ultra-convenient Telegram session that lets me throw in tasks from Telegram while I walk the dog in the park.
Although the last 3 tasks I threw in that way were done quite …. Anthropic has some problems with Opus's thinking.
Just imagine: Opus couldn't, on the second try, stand up a miserable GitHub Actions worker for a gitleaks scan and a couple of other ….
Or rather, it stood it up, spent 30 minutes per task, but the errors kept coming to my inbox as before.
Codex in 20 minutes found a heap of reasons why Claude failed and fixed them so that now everything works perfectly.
Some noticed that on Claude I burned through the entire $200 subscription + another $220 of credits on top. Imagine how much of this kind of thing I caught from Claude in that time?
Opus did NOT ONCE manage to even come close to GPT5.4 in quality of work, let alone overtake it in anything.
I was told Claude does design an order of magnitude better — total ….
Claude writes text better — total ….
Claude uses subagents better — total ….
Etc.
If the past week on my computer were a soccer match, Codex vs. Claude, the score is 100–0.
